newsitem.title: POLAND: WBK tender offer seen as formality.
newsitem.headline: WBK tender offer seen as formality.

text.p: Allied Irish Banks which seeks a majority stake in Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK) was bound by law to call a public tender to buy WBK shares but its price is likely to discourage any offers, analysts said.

AIB, which now has 45.7 percent of WBK has an option agreement with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) to buy all EBRD shares in WBK and gain a 60.2 percent control of the Polish bank.

AIB last month bought 9.4 percent of shares out of the EBRD portfolio at 13.95 zlotys and now was offering to buy all remaining WBK listed shares including the remaining 14.5 percent EBRD stake at 14 zlotys per share.

Analysts said the tender price, well below Wednesday's 18.2 zlotys, when WBK last traded before the tender announcement, showed AIB was not interested in boosting its WBK stake beyond the 60.2 percent level.
"It seems AIB doesn't intend to buy more than 60 percent," said Kamil Kalemba, a trader at ING Barings Securities.
Under Polish law any investor intending to gain a majority stake in a publicly traded company is obliged to call a public tender offer to buy all the remaining shares.
Analysts said the price set at the tender was within expectations and was unlikely to affect WBK performance on Tuesday. WBK trade was suspended on Monday.
